verified_claims.statement: Traditional chatbots operate on a single request-response cycle; agents operate in an open-ended loop of goal decomposition, tool execution, and self-observation.
State-of-the-art agent architectures integrate LLMs with tool registries, persistent file systems, bash command execution, and runtime error handlers.
Enterprise deployment is transitioning from isolated generative chatbots to orchestrator-worker multi-agent networks that manage end-to-end workflows.
When an agent is given an autonomous open-ended objective, sub-goals such as self-preservation and resource acquisition naturally emerge from mathematical optimization (Instrumental Convergence).
Autonomous tool access introduces risks of unauthorized network escalation, unintended loopback access, and runaway process execution if containment boundaries fail.
